design_references.title: Test quality and architectural fitness steering
design_references.claim: The Fleet CPG overlay can make structural fitness signals such as blast radius and change coupling available before an agent chooses a plan, enabling paired measurement of resulting structural debt.

hypothesis: Injecting CPG blast radius + change coupling into the ContextPacket pre-decision changes an agent's plan vs. control without it, yielding measurable reduction in structural debt (coupling, public surface growth).
null_hypothesis: Pre-decision CPG signals do not alter agent plan choice or resulting structural debt beyond random variance.
independent_variable: Availability of pre-decision CPG blast-radius and change-coupling context.

variants.name: control
variants.description: The agent receives the same frozen brownfield task and ContextPacket shape without CPG blast-radius or change-coupling context.

variants.name: treatment
variants.description: The agent receives the same task plus the pre-decision CPG blast-radius and change-coupling packet.

randomness.justification: Evaluating agent plan choice across 3 paired repetitions enables measuring plan-choice divergence and variance in structural-debt deltas.

metrics.primary: change in structural debt across paired patches, measured by coupling and public-surface growth
metrics.acceptance_rule: Report paired task-level deltas and dispersion. The benchmark supports the hypothesis only if treatment produces a measurable reduction in structural debt without a material loss of task completion; if plan choice and debt remain within the preregistered variance band, retain the null.

evaluator.rubric: For every paired task, verify that control and treatment use identical source, task, budget, and model settings; record whether the plan changes before implementation; compute coupling and public-surface growth from the resulting patches using the same CPG revision; inspect incomplete or stale graph scope as unknown rather than zero; and report task completion separately from structural-debt metrics. Reject a pair with missing terminal output, mismatched inputs, stale context, or an unbound evaluator.
